heading: Gratuity Tax Rules: Understanding Your Tax-Free Limit
tldr: Gratuity is a lump sum payment from an employer as a token of appreciation for long and dedicated service.
To be eligible, an employee typically needs to complete at least five years of continuous service with an organisation.
For most private sector employees, the maximum tax-exempt gratuity amount is ₹20 lakhs, as per government notification.
The actual tax-free portion depends on specific calculations based on service tenure and last drawn salary.
Gratuity received by Central, State, or Local Government employees is fully exempt from income tax.
caption:
Ever wondered about that lump sum you might get when you leave a job? It's called gratuity! If you've worked for a company for at least five years, you could be eligible. The best part? A big chunk of it, up to ₹20 lakhs for many, can be tax-free. Understanding these rules means more money stays in your pocket. Learn how it works in our latest article.
